# BPCS interlock record: template and worked example

## 1. How to use the template

- Keep one setpoint list per unit. Every value (setpoint, delay, timeout, deadband) has one row and one ID.
- Every other section, the configuration, the FAT sheets and the HMI text refer to the ID. They never repeat the value.
- Keep one interlock record per interlock. Name it IL-<unit>-NNN. Name its requirements FR-<module>-NNN.
- Put SIS functions in the SRS. Only reference them here (Section 1 of the record).
- Fill every section. Write "None" where a section does not apply, so a blank is never ambiguous.

## 2. Blank template

**Header**

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID / Title | IL-<unit>-NNN / <title> |
| Unit / Module | <unit> / <module tag> |
| Revision / Date / Status | <rev> / <date> / Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Built, FAT passed |
| Legacy source | <printout or C&E drawing, sheet, rung or block> |
| Classification | BPCS only. Related SIS function: <SRS ID or None> |
| Design basis | <hazard, consequence, HAZOP/LOPA node, risk reduction credited: yes/no> |
| Sign-off | Process: ___ Operations: ___ Controls: ___ |

**Section 1: Purpose and boundaries.** One paragraph. Name the upstream and downstream interfaces and the related SIS function.

**Section 2: Tags**

| Role (cause/effect/permissive/status) | Tag | New DCS point | Fail position or fail state | Instrument index ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**Section 3: Interlock row**

| Cause | Qualification | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method | Bypass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Section 4: Setpoint list** (the only place for values)

| ID | Description | Value | Units | Source | Status (final / confirm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Section 5: Abnormal handling**

| Condition | Interlock response | Effect on output | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bad PV | | | |
| Comms or I/O loss | | | |
| Power loss and restart | | | |
| Output fails to move | | | |
| Bypass active | | | |

**Section 6: Alarms and messages**

| Alarm tag | Condition | Priority (per alarm database) | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|

**Section 7: Operator interface.** List what the operator sees, changes, and is prompted for. Include the reset and bypass actions.

**Section 8: Requirements and FAT tests**

| ID | Requirement (testable, setpoints by ID) | FAT test: initial state, action, expected result |
|---|---|---|

**Section 9: Legacy traceability**

| Legacy item | New requirement | Difference or disposition |
|---|---|---|

**Section 10: Open items**

| # | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|

**Section 11: Change log** (use after construction starts, with MOC)

| Rev | Date | MOC # | Change | Approved by |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 3. Worked example: IL-H1100-001, low fuel gas pressure

I assumed the module is heater H-1100. I also assumed PT-1105 is upstream of XV-1106, and that XV-1106 is spring-return to closed. Open items 1 to 3 cover these assumptions.

**Header**

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID / Title | IL-H1100-001 / Low fuel gas pressure closes main fuel valve |
| Unit / Module | Heater unit / H-1100 fuel gas |
| Revision / Status | A / Draft |
| Legacy source | Old C&E drawing and logic printout. Sheet numbers to be added (open item 4) |
| Classification | BPCS only. Related SIS function: SRS ID TBD (open item 1) |
| Design basis | Low fuel gas pressure can cause flame instability and flame loss. Risk reduction credit in LOPA: confirm (open item 1) |
| Sign-off | Process: ___ Operations: ___ Controls: ___ |

**1. Purpose and boundaries.** This interlock closes the main fuel gas valve XV-1106 when fuel gas pressure at PT-1105 is low. It acts on XV-1106 only. It does not act on pilot gas or on other heater trips. Those are in the burner management function and the SRS.

**2. Tags**

| Role | Tag | Fail state | Instrument index ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cause | PT-1105 | Signal below the bad-PV limit is a fault | Instrument index, PT-1105 |
| Effect | XV-1106 | Spring return to closed | Instrument index, XV-1106 |
| Status | ZSC-1106 / ZSO-1106 | Not closed / not open is unknown | Instrument index (confirm tags, open item 3) |

**3. Interlock row**

| Cause | Qualification | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method | Bypass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PT-1105 below SP-1105-01 | For longer than SP-1105-04 | Close XV-1106 | Latched | Operator reset on H-1100 faceplate, only when PT-1105 is above SP-1105-03 | Maintenance bypass, limited by SP-1105-07 |
| PT-1105 bad PV (outside SP-1105-05 limits) | For longer than SP-1105-04 | Close XV-1106 | Latched | Same as above | Same as above |

**4. Setpoint list**

| ID | Description | Value | Units | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-1105-01 | PT-1105 low trip | 10 | psig | Provisional | confirm |
| SP-1105-02 | PT-1105 low alarm (PAL-1105) | 15 | psig | Provisional | confirm |
| SP-1105-03 | PT-1105 reset permissive (above trip) | 13 | psig | Provisional | confirm |
| SP-1105-04 | Trip on-delay | 2 | s | Provisional | confirm |
| SP-1105-05 | PT-1105 bad-PV low limit | 3.6 | mA | Provisional | confirm |
| SP-1105-06 | XV-1106 travel-time limit | 10 | s | Provisional | confirm |
| SP-1105-07 | Maintenance bypass maximum duration | 8 | h | Provisional | confirm |

**5. Abnormal handling**

| Condition | Interlock response | Effect on output | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bad PV | Treat as a trip condition | Close XV-1106 | Reset after the signal is good and above SP-1105-03 |
| Comms or I/O loss | Output module de-energizes | XV-1106 closes (fail closed) | Reset after comms return and the permissive is met |
| Power loss and restart | Interlock starts in the tripped state | XV-1106 stays closed | Operator reset needed. No automatic reopen |
| XV-1106 does not close within SP-1105-06 | Alarm | Output stays at closed command | Operator checks the valve in the field |
| Bypass active | Interlock does not act. Bypass alarm shows | None | Bypass ends at SP-1105-07 or on operator cancel. If the trip condition exists then, the trip occurs |

**6. Alarms and messages**

| Alarm tag | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| PAL-1105 | PT-1105 below SP-1105-02 | Per alarm database (provisional: medium, confirm) | Check the fuel gas supply. Reduce heater firing if needed |
| IL-H1100-001 TRIPPED | Interlock latched | Per alarm database (provisional: high, confirm) | Find the cause. Reset only when the reset permissive is met |
| IL-H1100-001 BYPASSED | Bypass active | Per alarm database (provisional: medium, confirm) | Confirm that the bypass is still needed |
| XV-1106 TRAVEL FAIL | Travel time above SP-1105-06 | Per alarm database (provisional: high, confirm) | Send an operator to check XV-1106 |
| PT-1105 BAD PV | Signal outside SP-1105-05 limit | Per alarm database (provisional: high, confirm) | Call instrument technician |

**7. Operator interface.** The H-1100 faceplate shows PT-1105, XV-1106 position, interlock state (normal, tripped, bypassed) and the reset permissive. The operator can push RESET, but only when the permissive is met. A user with engineer rights can set or cancel the bypass. The operator cannot give an open command to XV-1106 while the interlock is tripped.

**8. Requirements and FAT tests**

| ID | Requirement | FAT test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-H1100-001 | The BPCS closes XV-1106 when PT-1105 is below SP-1105-01 for longer than SP-1105-04. | Start: XV-1106 open, PT-1105 above SP-1105-02. Simulate PT-1105 below SP-1105-01. Expect: XV-1106 closes after SP-1105-04. Not before. |
| FR-H1100-002 | The trip stays latched after PT-1105 recovers. | After 001, raise PT-1105 above SP-1105-03. Expect: XV-1106 stays closed. State stays tripped. |
| FR-H1100-003 | The BPCS accepts RESET only when PT-1105 is above SP-1105-03. | Push RESET with PT-1105 between SP-1105-01 and SP-1105-03. Expect: rejected. Raise PT-1105 above SP-1105-03 and push RESET. Expect: accepted. |
| FR-H1100-004 | The BPCS blocks every open command to XV-1106 while the interlock is tripped. | Give an open command from the faceplate and from a sequence. Expect: both blocked. XV-1106 stays closed. |
| FR-H1100-005 | The BPCS treats a PT-1105 signal outside the SP-1105-05 limit as a trip condition. | Simulate PT-1105 signal below SP-1105-05. Expect: XV-1106 closes after SP-1105-04. PT-1105 BAD PV alarm shows. |
| FR-H1100-006 | The BPCS raises PAL-1105 when PT-1105 is below SP-1105-02. | Lower PT-1105 below SP-1105-02, above SP-1105-01. Expect: PAL-1105 on. No trip. |
| FR-H1100-007 | The BPCS raises XV-1106 TRAVEL FAIL if XV-1106 is not closed within SP-1105-06 of a trip. | Hold the ZSC-1106 simulation off. Trip the interlock. Expect: alarm after SP-1105-06. |
| FR-H1100-008 | XV-1106 goes to closed on loss of the controller output or I/O comms. | Remove the output module. Expect: XV-1106 de-energizes and closes. |
| FR-H1100-009 | After a controller restart, the interlock starts tripped and XV-1106 stays closed. | Power-cycle the controller with XV-1106 open and PT-1105 normal. Expect: XV-1106 closed, state tripped. Reset needed. |
| FR-H1100-010 | The bypass ends at SP-1105-07. If a trip condition exists then, the BPCS trips. | Set the bypass. Lower PT-1105 below SP-1105-01. Expect: no trip, bypass alarm on. Advance the bypass timer to SP-1105-07. Expect: trip. |
| FR-H1100-011 | The BPCS records each trip, reset, and bypass change in the event log with a time stamp. | After tests 001, 003 and 010, read the event log. Expect: one entry per event, correct order. |

**9. Legacy traceability**

| Legacy item | New requirement | Difference |
|---|---|---|
| C&E row for low fuel gas pressure (sheet TBD) | FR-H1100-001, -002 | Legacy trip value to be compared with SP-1105-01 (open item 2) |
| Legacy reset logic (rung TBD) | FR-H1100-003, -004 | Confirm whether the legacy reset was automatic |
| None found | FR-H1100-005, -007, -009, -010 | New behavior. Operations must approve |

**10. Open items**

| # | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm that no SIS function covers low fuel gas pressure. Add the SRS ID, or confirm that no LOPA credit is taken here. | Process safety engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| 2 | Replace all provisional values in the setpoint list with the legacy and process-confirmed values. | Process engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| 3 | Confirm that PT-1105 is upstream of XV-1106, that XV-1106 is spring-return to closed, and the ZSC/ZSO tags. | Instrument engineer | 2026-11-06 |
| 4 | Add the legacy sheet and rung references to the header and Section 9. | Controls engineer | 2026-11-06 |
| 5 | Confirm the effect on pilot gas and other heater trips. | Process safety engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| 6 | Obtain operations sign-off on states, prompts, reset and bypass. | Operations lead | 2026-11-20 |
| 7 | Confirm alarm priorities against the rationalized alarm database. | Alarm system owner | 2026-11-20 |

**11. Change log:** none. Rev A is the first issue.

## 4. Notes for the 40-unit rollout

- If the SRS already has a low fuel gas pressure trip for each heater, this BPCS record is a separate layer. Keep it separate and do not claim risk reduction for it unless the LOPA credits it.
- Have the configurer read the setpoint list into the DCS as parameters by ID, or generate the config from it. Do the same for the FAT sheets. That is what stops the five-copy problem.
- Do the STE pass on Sections 1, 5, 7 and 8 only after the engineering content is final.
